mainTopic: Laws of פסולי המוקדשין: redeeming their offspring, slaughtering them outside, and why a תמורה made after redemption must die
overview: This amud finishes an earlier derivation: a word in the פסוק adds the milk of redeemed פסולי המוקדשין to the prohibition. The גמרא then reads a ברייתא closely. Its wording seems to imply that blemished offspring can be redeemed, which would disprove רב הונא. רב הונא answers that the wording was only copied from the first half of the ברייתא. Next, רב הונא's version of the ברייתא makes one who slaughters these animals outside the עזרה liable, but only in the narrow case of a tiny eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. רב נחמן rules that a תמורה made after the animal was redeemed must die, because it can neither be offered nor redeemed. אביי defends this against רב עמרם's comparison to the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר: each תמורה follows the animal it replaced. A ברייתא supports רב נחמן from the פסוק about animals that chew the cud. The גמרא then works out how that פסוק and a tradition both relate to the five חטאות that are left to die. The amud ends by opening a new משנה about a Jew who receives צאן ברזל from a גוי.

steps.title: A word in the verse comes to include the milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. A word in the פסוק teaches that the milk of a redeemed disqualified consecrated animal is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to include its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: This line wraps up the earlier discussion, which carried over from the previous section. It explains that an extra word in the פסוק comes to forbid the animal's milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after a disqualified consecrated animal is redeemed, some benefits from it stay forbidden. This line adds that its milk is included in that prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to bring in something extra
Its milk

phrases.english: To include its milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the derivation carried over from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The milk of redeemed פסולי המוקדשין is also forbidden.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא and drawing two inferences
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling on offspring of animals that were consecrated before they got a blemish. It then reads two inferences from the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: unblemished offspring cannot be redeemed, and you cannot dedicate them as any offering you want. The inferences: only unblemished ones cannot be redeemed, so blemished ones can be. And only 'any offering you want' is not allowed, so dedicating them as the same offering as the mother is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ברייתא it quoted earlier. It reads each of its two phrases closely to see what they imply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'unblemished,' which suggests that blemished offspring are different and can be redeemed. It also says 'any offering he desires,' which suggests that dedicating them as the mother's own type of offering is allowed. These two inferences will be used against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the formula for re-quoting a ברייתא already cited
Redeemed, taken out of קדושה by exchanging them for money
Unblemished animals
Blemished animals
Dedicate them, attach קדושה to them as an offering
They are redeemed (Aramaic)

phrases.english: The Master said:
They are not redeemed while unblemished,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the offspring of consecrated animals that were consecrated first and only got a blemish later.

phrases.english: and one may not dedicate them as any offering he wishes.
It is unblemished ones that are not redeemed,
which implies that blemished ones are redeemed.
It is as any offering he wishes that one may not dedicate them,
which implies that as that same offering, one may dedicate them.
phrases.notes: "That same offering" means the same kind of offering the mother was consecrated as.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a fresh analysis of the ברייתא after closing the previous derivation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unblemished offspring are not redeemed and cannot be dedicated as any offering. By inference, blemished ones may be redeemed, and they may be dedicated as the mother's offering.

steps.title: How do both inferences fit one case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what real situation the two inferences describe together.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you find this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for a concrete case that combines both inferences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two inferences seem to pull in different directions. One treats the offspring as holy enough to dedicate. The other treats it as redeemable. The גמרא wants to show how both can be true in a single case.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? A request for a concrete case

phrases.english: How can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two inferences from step 2 combine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case in which both inferences apply.

steps.title: Dedicated as the same offering, redeemed once blemished
steps.stepSummary: The case: the offspring is dedicated as the mother's offering, and if it gets a blemish it can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where one dedicates them as that same offering, and they are redeemed once they have a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by joining the two inferences into one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the offspring can be dedicated as the same offering as its mother. If it later becomes blemished, it can be redeemed like any blemished offering. This means the offspring is not simply left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: With their blemish, once they become blemished

phrases.english: Where one dedicates them as that same offering,
and they are redeemed with their blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dedicate the offspring as the mother's offering, and redeem it once it becomes blemished.

steps.title: Does this refute רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this reading of the ברייתא disproves רב הונא, who holds that such offspring cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. The inferences from the ברייתא seem to contradict רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא held that these offspring are never redeemed and must be left to die. The inference that blemished offspring can be redeemed directly contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? An opening for a suggested conclusion
A refutation; a strong challenge from a תנאי source

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case built in step 4 against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that offspring of פסולי המוקדשין cannot be redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that blemished offspring can be redeemed, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: The wording only mirrors the first half
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that blemished offspring cannot be redeemed either. The ברייתא's second half simply copied the wording of the first half, so no inference can be drawn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: the same is true even for blemished ones, they are not redeemed. Since the first half taught 'redeemed unblemished,' the second half also taught 'not redeemed unblemished.' And since the first half taught 'as any offering he wishes,' the second half also taught 'as any offering he wishes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. He says the inferences rest on wording that was chosen only to match the first half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא (the case of a blemish that came before consecration) needed the words 'unblemished' and 'any offering.' The סיפא repeated the same words just to keep the two halves parallel. So the words carry no extra lesson, and the inferences fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you: a defense offered on someone's behalf
The same law applies
Since; because of the parallel wording
The first clause
The latter clause

steps.whatToRemember: An inference drawn from a ברייתא's wording can be rejected by saying the wording was only borrowed to match the other half (אַיְּידֵי). רב הונא stands: these offspring are not redeemed, even with a blemish.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying unblemished offspring can be redeemed. He means that the word 'unblemished' teaches nothing on its own, so blemished offspring cannot be redeemed either.

phrases.english: רב הונא can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אֵין נִפְדִּין,
phrases.english: The same is true, that even blemished ones are not redeemed,
and since the first clause taught 'they are redeemed unblemished,'
the latter clause also taught 'they are not redeemed unblemished,'
and since the first clause taught 'as any offering he wishes,'
the latter clause also taught 'as any offering he wishes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אֵין נִפְדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel wording (אַיְּידֵי): the words of the סיפא were borrowed from the רישא, so no inference can be drawn from them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'unblemished' and 'any offering' were chosen on purpose, which implies blemished offspring can be redeemed and can be dedicated as the same offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words only mirror the רישא. Blemished offspring are not redeemed either, so רב הונא's view stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: an inference from wording can be cancelled by showing the wording was there only for symmetry.

steps.title: Slaughtering them outside brings no punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: one who slaughters these animals outside the עזרה is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next piece of the ברייתא. It is setting up רב הונא's different version, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals now have a blemish, so they can no longer go on the מזבח. Slaughtering an animal outside the עזרה is only punished when the animal could have been offered inside. That is why the ברייתא says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה, which is normally punished with כרת
Exempt; no punishment
Outside (the Temple courtyard)

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the animals that were consecrated first and only later got a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא after רב הונא's defense in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering these blemished consecrated animals outside the עזרה brings no punishment.

steps.title: רב הונא reads it as liable, for a tiny eye blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's version says חייב. He applies it to a tiny blemish on the cornea, following רבי עקיבא, who holds that such an animal stays on the מזבח once it was brought up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא teaches it as 'liable,' and he explains it as dealing with tiny blemishes on the cornea of the eye, following רבי עקיבא, who says: if they went up onto the altar, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא has a different wording of the ברייתא: 'חייב' instead of 'פטור'. He explains which case that wording must be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny eye blemish does not fully disqualify the animal for רבי עקיבא. If it was already put on the מזבח, it is offered. Because the animal is still partly fit for the מזבח, slaughtering it outside counts as שחוטי חוץ and brings liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (a version of the text)
Tiny blemishes on the cornea of the eye
If they went up onto the מזבח, they are not taken down
Following the view of

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's version really does say חייב, not פטור. But he limits it to a very narrow case: a tiny eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. He is not saying that slaughtering any blemished animal outside brings liability.

phrases.english: Rav Huna teaches it as 'liable,'
and he sets it in the case of tiny blemishes on the cornea,
and according to Rabbi Akiva, who says:
If they went up, they do not come down.
phrases.notes: If such a blemished animal was already put on the מזבח, it stays there and is offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different wording of the clause quoted in step 7, together with the narrow case that wording must be about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב הונא's version, slaughtering outside makes one liable. That applies to an animal with a tiny eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: They make a תמורה before or after redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's next ruling: these animals can make a תמורה both before and after their redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether before its redemption or after its redemption, it makes a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the ברייתא. This sets up רב נחמן's comment about a תמורה made after redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals were consecrated before they had a blemish, so their holiness is strong. Even after redemption, some of it stays. Because of that, an animal swapped for them still becomes holy as a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tries to swap for a consecrated animal; it becomes holy too
Redemption: transferring an animal's holiness onto money

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ
phrases.english: whether before its redemption or after its redemption,
it makes a substitute.
phrases.notes: In other words, an animal someone tries to swap for it becomes holy too.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal consecrated before its blemish makes a valid תמורה both before and after its redemption.

steps.title: A תמורה made after redemption must die
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that a תמורה made after the redemption is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: and its substitute made after its redemption must die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a ruling about the ברייתא's case. The תמורה does become holy, but nothing can be done with it, so it is left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only told us that the תמורה becomes holy. רב נחמן adds what happens to it next: it is not offered, not redeemed, and not eaten. It is left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: It dies; it is locked away until it dies

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nahman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
And its substitute made after its redemption must die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule to the ברייתא's clause quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה made after the original animal was redeemed is left to die.

steps.title: Why must it die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this תמורה has to die. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting a holy animal die is an unusual outcome. The גמרא wants to know why no better option is available.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a תמורה made after redemption must be left to die.

steps.title: It can neither be offered nor redeemed
steps.stepSummary: It cannot be offered, because its holiness comes from holiness that was pushed aside. It cannot be redeemed, because its holiness is too weak to pass onto money. So it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we do with it? Offer it? It comes from the power of holiness that was pushed aside. Redeem it? Its holiness is not strong enough to pass onto redemption money. Therefore it dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the options one by one and shows that each one fails. The only thing left is to let it die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Its 'mother' was already redeemed, so that animal's holiness for the מזבח had been pushed aside (קדושה דחויה). The תמורה gets its holiness from that pushed-aside holiness, so it cannot go on the מזבח. Its holiness is also too weak to pass onto money, so redemption does not work either.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that was pushed aside and can no longer be used for the מזבח
It is not strong enough
To pass its holiness onto its redemption money
Therefore

phrases.english: What should we do?
Offer it? It comes from the power of pushed-aside holiness,
phrases.notes: Its 'mother' was already redeemed, so that animal's holiness for the מזבח had been pushed aside.

phrases.english: Redeem it? It is not strong enough to take hold on its redemption money,
therefore it dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Offering it fails because of קדושה דחויה, and redemption fails because its holiness is too weak. That leaves only death.

steps.title: רב עמרם: let the owners eat it with its blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם objects: let the owners eat it once it has a blemish, just like the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר. A משנה teaches that those are eaten with their blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם objected: Let it be eaten with its blemish by the owners! What is the difference between this and the substitute of a בכור or מעשר animal? As we learned: the substitute of a בכור or מעשר animal, they, their offspring, and their offspring's offspring until the end of the world, are like a בכור or מעשר animal and are eaten with their blemish by the owners!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם challenges the ruling that it must die. He points to a third option the גמרא did not consider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that a תמורה can be eaten with its blemish without any redemption: that is the rule for the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר. If so, why not do the same here instead of letting the animal die?

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it
Firstborn animal
Animal tithe (מעשר בהמה)
In its blemished state
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rav Amram objected to it:
But let it be eaten with its blemish by the owners!
For what is the difference between this
and the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal?
As we learned: the substitute of a firstborn or tithe animal,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת תמורה.

phrases.english: they, their offspring, and their offspring's offspring
until the end of the whole world
they are like a firstborn or tithe animal,
and are eaten with their blemish by the owners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 12 that the תמורה must die.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a תמורה made after redemption must die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תמורה of a בכור or מעשר is eaten with its blemish without redemption. So this תמורה should also be eaten, not left to die.

steps.title: אביי: each תמורה follows its mother
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a תמורה carries the name of the animal it replaced. A בכור or מעשר is itself eaten with its blemish, so its תמורה is too. That does not apply here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: This one bears its mother's name and that one bears its mother's name. This one is called entirely 'a substitute of a firstborn or tithe.' Just as a firstborn or tithe is eaten with its blemish by the owners, so too their substitute is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב נחמן's ruling. He shows that the case of בכור and מעשר is different from our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה follows the rules of the animal it was swapped for. A blemished בכור or מעשר is eaten by its owners without redemption, so its תמורה is eaten the same way. Our תמורה carries the name of a different kind of holy animal, one that is not eaten that way, so it gets no such permission. That leaves רב נחמן's ruling in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It carries its 'mother's' name, meaning the status of the animal it replaced
It is called
They are eaten

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה follows the rules of the animal it replaced. The תמורה of a בכור or מעשר is eaten with its blemish, because those animals themselves are eaten that way. A תמורה made after redemption from other קדשים is left to die.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
This one bears its mother's name
phrases.notes: 'Mother' here means the animal it was swapped for, not the animal that gave birth to it.

phrases.english: and that one bears its mother's name;

phrases.aramaic: זֶה כּוּלּוֹ תְּמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר מִיקַּרְיָא,
phrases.english: this one is called entirely 'a substitute of a firstborn or tithe,'
just as a firstborn or tithe, in their blemished state,
are eaten by the owners,
so too their substitute is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: a תמורה follows the status of the animal it replaced.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every blemished תמורה can be eaten by its owners, like the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a תמורה of a בכור or מעשר is eaten with its blemish, because those animals themselves are. Our תמורה cannot be eaten, so it dies.

steps.title: אביי finishes: this תמורה is called a holy animal's substitute and cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: אביי applies his rule to our case. The תמורה is called 'the תמורה of holy animals.' Holy animals are eaten only through redemption, and this one is too weak to be redeemed, so it can never be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this animal also carries its mother's name: it is called 'the substitute of holy animals.' Just as holy animals can only be eaten through redemption, their substitutes can also only be eaten through redemption. But this one is not strong enough for its holiness to pass onto redemption money.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer to רב עמרם by showing what 'carrying the original animal's name' means in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה of a בכור is named after a בכור, so it is eaten with its blemish just like a בכור. Our תמורה is named after 'holy animals,' and holy animals are eaten only after redemption. Step 12 already said this תמורה's holiness is too weak to be redeemed, so the one way to permit it is closed, and it must die.

keyTerms.meaning: It carries its mother's name: the תמורה is treated like the animal it replaced
Redemption: moving an animal's holiness onto money so the animal may be eaten
It is not strong enough
To 'grab' or pass onto: here, for the holiness to transfer to the money

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה follows the name of what it replaced. Here that name is 'holy animals,' which need redemption, and redemption is impossible. So it dies.

phrases.english: And this one carries its mother's name:
phrases.notes: 'Mother' here means the original animal it replaced, not a real mother.

phrases.english: it is called 'the substitute of holy animals.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה קָדָשִׁים לָא מִיתַּכְלִי אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן —
phrases.english: Just as holy animals are eaten only through redemption,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּמוּרָתָן נָמֵי לָא מִיתַּכְלִי אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן,
phrases.english: so too their substitutes are also eaten only through redemption.
But this one is not strong enough to pass onto its redemption money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 14 by applying the 'name' rule to our case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the name this תמורה carries leads to a different result than a בכור's תמורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב עמרם thought every תמורה could be eaten with a blemish, like the תמורה of a בכור or מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תמורה is named after holy animals, which need redemption. It cannot be redeemed, so it can never be eaten.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן from the פסוק about animals that chew the cud
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks where we learn that the תמורה of disqualified holy animals must die. It answers from the פסוק 'of those that chew the cud... impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רב נחמן: From where do we know that the substitute of disqualified holy animals dies? The verse says: 'Of those that chew the cud... impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב נחמן and roots it in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ruled that a תמורה made after redemption dies. The ברייתא gives that same ruling a source in the Torah: the word 'טמא' in the פסוק about animals that chew the cud. It is read to include an animal that looks kosher but still may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that matches his view
Holy animals that became disqualified (because of a blemish) and were redeemed
Animals that chew the cud
The verse teaches

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב נחמן:
From where do we know that the substitute of disqualified holy animals dies?
The verse says:
'Of those that chew the cud... impure.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״א. The word 'impure' is read to include this kosher-looking animal that still can't be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב נחמן's reasoning, the גמרא brings outside support from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a תמורה made after redemption is left to die.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה... טָמֵא' (ויקרא י״א:ד).

steps.title: Isn't that פסוק needed for the five חטאות that die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this extra word is already used to teach the law of the five חטאות that are left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for the five sin offerings that are left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's use of the פסוק. It says the פסוק is already being used for another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word in the Torah usually teaches one thing. If 'טמא' here teaches about the five חטאות that die, it cannot also be the source for the תמורה of disqualified holy animals.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
The five kinds of חטאת that are left to die (such as the offspring of a חטאת or a חטאת whose owner died)

phrases.english: But this is needed
for the five sin offerings that are left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְחָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in the ברייתא of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה... טָמֵא' as the source for the תמורה of disqualified holy animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That word is already used for the five חטאות that die, so it is not free to teach this law too.

steps.title: The five חטאות come from the split-hoof phrase instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the five חטאות are learned from a different phrase: 'of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That law comes from 'of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving the five חטאות a different source in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two 'impure' phrases: one about chewing the cud and one about the split hoof. The split-hoof phrase teaches the five חטאות. That leaves the cud-chewing phrase free for the תמורה of disqualified holy animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that have a split hoof
It is learned (literally, 'it comes out') from

phrases.english: That one is learned from 'of those that have a split hoof... impure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning sources: each 'impure' phrase teaches a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cud-chewing phrase was needed for the five חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split-hoof phrase teaches the five חטאות, so the cud-chewing phrase is free for רב נחמן's case.

steps.title: A second ברייתא confirms the five חטאות come from the split-hoof phrase
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא states that the five חטאות that die are learned from 'of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: From where do we know about the five sin offerings that are left to die? The verse says: 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 could look like a guess made up to dodge the question. This ברייתא shows that a teaching already learned the five חטאות from the split-hoof phrase, which supports that answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
From where (do we know this)?

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
From where do we know about the five sin offerings that are left to die?
The verse says: 'Of those that have a split hoof... impure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 18 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the five חטאות are learned from the split-hoof phrase.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'מִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה... טָמֵא' as the source for the five חטאות.

steps.title: But the five חטאות are a tradition, not a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the second ברייתא. The five חטאות that die are known from a tradition, so no פסוק is needed for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the five sin offerings that are left to die are a law we learned as a tradition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא it just quoted. It points out that the five חטאות are known from a tradition, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a law is already known from a tradition, the Torah does not need a פסוק to teach it. So the split-hoof phrase cannot really be for the five חטאות, and the גמרא must explain what it actually teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A הלכה: a law handed down by tradition
We learned it by tradition

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting the law of the five חטאות. Everyone agrees they die. The question is only where the law comes from: a tradition, not a פסוק.

phrases.english: The five sin offerings that are left to die
are a law we learned as a tradition!

steps.triggerLanguage: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the five חטאות come from the split-hoof phrase.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law already known by tradition needs no פסוק, so that phrase must be teaching something else.

steps.title: The פסוק actually comes for the תמורה of an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the ברייתא. The פסוק actually comes to teach the law of the תמורה of an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when the verse came, it came for the substitute of a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by giving the split-hoof phrase a new job: teaching about the תמורה of an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the five חטאות are known by tradition, the phrase is free. The גמרא says it teaches the law of a תמורה of an אשם, which cannot be brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introducing a new explanation)
When the verse came (this is what it came to teach)
The substitute of an אשם (guilt offering)

phrases.english: Rather, when the verse came,
it came for the substitute of a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא קְרָא לִתְמוּרַת אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of what the פסוק teaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split-hoof phrase was for the five חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five חטאות are a tradition. The phrase teaches about the תמורה of an אשם.

steps.title: The תמורה of an אשם is also known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again. The law of the תמורה of an אשם is also a tradition, from the rule: whatever dies in a חטאת grazes in an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the substitute of a guilt offering is also a law known by tradition: whatever is left to die in the case of a sin offering is left to graze in the case of a guilt offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. It points out that the תמורה of an אשם is also already known from a tradition. In the next step the גמרא accepts this and drops the אשם reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition says every case where a חטאת dies matches a case where an אשם grazes. A תמורה of a חטאת dies, so a תמורה of an אשם must graze. That means no פסוק is needed for it, and the phrase is free again.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes: it is left in the pasture until it gets a blemish, instead of being brought as a קרבן
The rule: whatever dies in the case of a חטאת grazes in the case of an אשם

steps.confusionAlert: 'Grazes' does not mean the animal is fine to use. It is left out to pasture until it gets a blemish, but it is not brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: The substitute of a guilt offering is also a law known by tradition:
whatever is left to die in the case of a sin offering
is left to graze in the case of a guilt offering!
phrases.notes: Since a חטאת's תמורה dies, this rule already tells us an אשם's תמורה grazes, so no פסוק is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the split-hoof phrase teaches the law of the תמורה of an אשם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule 'whatever dies in a חטאת grazes in an אשם' already gives this law by tradition, so the פסוק would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Both the verse and the tradition are needed for the five sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to saying the פסוק is about the five חטאות המתות. Both the פסוק and the הלכה are needed: the הלכה teaches that they die, and the פסוק teaches that eating them breaks a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק really is about the five חטאות that die. We need both the פסוק and the tradition. With only the פסוק, I would think they are left to graze, so the tradition teaches that they are left to die. With only the tradition, I would think that someone who ate from them broke a prohibition but not a לאו, so the פסוק teaches that there is a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 20 that the five חטאות are already known from a tradition. It says each source teaches something the other one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said that if a הלכה למשה מסיני covers the five חטאות, the פסוק adds nothing. The answer splits the jobs. The tradition tells us what to do with the animal (it is left to die, not to graze). The פסוק tells us how serious it is to eat it: a real לאו, not just a general איסור. This also removes the need for the reading from Step 21 about the תמורה of an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (it does not mean 'forever' here)
It is needed
A הלכה known by tradition, not from a פסוק
Left to graze (until it gets a blemish)
A general prohibition, less severe than a לאו
A negative commandment of the Torah; breaking it brings מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'לְעוֹלָם' does not mean 'forever.' It means 'actually, really.' The גמרא is going back to its first idea after testing another one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic 'צריכותא' pattern. When a law has two sources, the גמרא shows that each source adds something unique, so neither one is extra.

phrases.english: Rather, [the verse] actually [refers to] the five sin offerings that die,
and the verse is needed, and the tradition is needed.
For if [we had it only] from the verse, I would have said [they are left] to graze;
the tradition teaches us [that they are left] to die.
And if [we had it only] from the tradition, I would have said:
where one happened to go and eat
from these five sin offerings —
there is a prohibition, but there is no negative commandment;
[so the verse] teaches us that there is a negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, וְאִצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא וְאִצְטְרִיךְ הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 22 rejected the תמורת אשם reading, the גמרא goes back to the plain reading of the ברייתא and answers the objection from Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: both sources are needed, and each teaches something different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the פסוק: the animals graze. With only the הלכה: eating them is an איסור without a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה teaches that they are left to die. The פסוק teaches that eating them breaks a לאו.

steps.title: The verse links two items so both are left to die
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the פסוק is not needed for the five חטאות themselves. It puts something learned from 'those that chew the cud' side by side with the five חטאות learned from 'those that have a split hoof,' so the first item is also left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: the פסוק compares the thing learned from 'those that chew the cud' to the thing learned from 'those that have a split hoof.' Just as there the animal is left to die, so too here it is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same challenge. It agrees the five חטאות are known from tradition, but says the פסוק is used to make a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer the five חטאות still come from the tradition, so the 'split hoof' phrase is free for another job. The item learned from 'those that chew the cud' is the תמורה of פסולי המוקדשין (Step 16). The פסוק places it next to the five חטאות, so it shares their law: it is left to die, not to graze. This brings the sugya back to support רב נחמן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
To compare: linking two things because the Torah placed them together (a הקש)
Animals that chew the cud
Animals that have a split hoof
Just as there, so too here: the formula for carrying a law from one case to another

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the פסוק is needed. (1) It adds a לאו for eating the five חטאות, while the tradition teaches that they die. (2) It compares the תמורה of פסולי המוקדשין to the five חטאות, so that תמורה is also left to die, just as רב נחמן ruled.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
[the verse comes] to compare an item that comes from "those that chew the cud"
phrases.notes: This is the תמורה of disqualified holy animals, which the ברייתא in Step 16 learned from 'chew the cud.'

phrases.english: with an item that comes from "those that have a split hoof":
phrases.notes: This means the five חטאות, which were learned from 'split hoof' back in Steps 18–19.

phrases.english: just as there, [the animal is left] to die,
so too here, [the animal is left] to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְאַקּוֹשֵׁי דָּבָר הַבָּא מִמַּעֲלֵי גֵּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the challenge in Step 20, alongside the answer in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a הקש (comparison)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the five חטאות are known from tradition, the 'split hoof' phrase seems to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links the item from 'those that chew the cud' to the five חטאות, so it shares their law of being left to die.

steps.title: New משנה: receiving a guaranteed-investment flock from a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It discusses someone who receives צאן ברזל (animals with a guaranteed value) from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who receives צאן ברזל from a גוי...
steps.whatsHappening: The previous discussion is finished, and a new משנה begins. This line only opens the case; the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In צאן ברזל, the Jew raises the גוי's animals and promises to pay a fixed value even if they die, and the babies are split between them. This shared ownership will matter for the law of בכורה, because a firstborn is only holy if a Jew owns it. The question will be who counts as the owner here.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: 'our משנה,' marking the start of a new משנה
One who receives / takes on
'Iron sheep': animals taken to raise with a guaranteed value the receiver must pay back, even if they die
A non-Jew

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete sentence. It only sets up the case. The ruling about the babies and בכורה comes next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who receives a guaranteed-investment flock from a gentile —
phrases.notes: The Jew raises the animals and owes a fixed value no matter what happens, and they split the babies.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַבֵּל צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ends; it does not depend on the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the case of a Jew who takes צאן ברזל from a גוי. The ruling about בכורה follows in the continuation.
